# Protocol & Lifecycle Requirements Quality Checklist: MCP 2026-07-28 R1 Native Isolation

**Purpose**: Formal release-gate review of the R1 protocol, compatibility, lifecycle, and customer-evidence requirements before implementation acceptance.  
**Created**: 2026-08-31  
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the pre-owner-election selection, immutable owner-era, and zero-value legacy-default requirements specified as one complete admission boundary? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001; Public Policy §Library caller contract]
- [x] CHK002 Are protocol era and sharing policy defined as independent dimensions, including an unambiguous forced-isolation requirement for every R1 modern owner? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003; Data Model §Independent state domains]
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements present for both modern/legacy identity separation and byte-stable legacy identity, including the supported Windows and Unix IPC-path constraint? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, FR-009; Daemon Control §Identity and owner election requirements]
- [x] CHK004 Do the ingress requirements cover every stated invalid opening class—missing, null, non-object, malformed, unsupported, conflicting, and ambiguous metadata—before any start or attach side effect? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005; Public Policy §Failure result]
- [x] CHK005 Are the no-bootstrap, no-cache, no-template, no-list/list-change, and no-replay requirements explicit for both the first modern opening and later reconnect/lifecycle paths? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007; Lifecycle Quarantine §Universal modern invariants]
- [x] CHK006 Are native modern directionality, MRTR opaque-state handling, request-scoped logging, and single-recipient routing each specified without introducing an unapproved shared-correlation authority? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, FR-011; Research §R-06, R-07]

## Requirement Clarity and Error Semantics

- [x] CHK007 Is the required modern metadata shape sufficiently specified to distinguish absent, null, non-object, malformed, and valid-empty client-capability declarations, while keeping `clientInfo` optional? [Clarity, Public Policy §Library caller contract; Research §R-04]
- [x] CHK008 Do requirements unambiguously partition malformed metadata (`-32602`), valid unsupported versions (`-32022` plus `supported` and `requested`), and local admission/control failures? [Clarity, Public Policy §Failure result; Daemon Control §Error contract]
- [x] CHK009 Is it explicit which refusals must occur before daemon spawn, owner election, IPC attachment, or legacy fallback, rather than merely requiring a generic failure? [Clarity, Daemon Control §Required spawn state machine; Spec §Verification scenarios and acceptance evidence]
- [x] CHK010 Is the exact modern control-echo rule clear about response success, syntax, equality, modern isolated target, and the fail-closed consequence of absent, old, unknown, or mismatched values? [Clarity, Daemon Control §Echo validation at the shim]
- [x] CHK011 Are error and status diagnostic-redaction requirements defined for all stated admission and lifecycle error classes without conflating local safety failure with a protocol-version error? [Clarity, Lifecycle Quarantine §Boundary error behavior; Daemon Control §Error contract]

## Consistency and Legacy Parity

- [x] CHK012 Do the explicit-modern selection requirements remain consistent with the prohibition on deriving protocol era from historical sharing flags, `clientInfo`, discovery, upstream capabilities, or failed requests? [Consistency, Public Policy §Public policy values, §CLI caller contract; Research §R-02]
- [x] CHK013 Are the native pass-through requirement and the no-translation exclusion consistent across methods, results, errors, initialization behavior, callbacks, and dual-era fallback? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, FR-006; Spec §Out of scope]
- [x] CHK014 Does every modern safety restriction identify legacy behavior as retained rather than accidentally changing legacy initialization, cache, template, replay, reconnect, identity, or lifecycle semantics? [Consistency, Spec §Legacy native path; Lifecycle Quarantine §Legacy compatibility]
- [x] CHK015 Are the requirements consistent that `server/discover` may be a host-sent opener but is neither mandatory nor mux-injected as a synthetic handshake? [Consistency, Public Policy §CLI caller contract; Research §R-06]
- [x] CHK016 Do the R1 isolation and sole-recipient logging requirements remain consistent with the exclusion of shared logging attribution and modern owner sharing? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §Out of scope; Research §R-07]

## Native Protocol Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Are primary-path requirements specified for both a direct ordinary valid modern request and a host-originated `server/discover` opening message, with byte-preserved opening content? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §User Story 1; Quickstart §Scenario 1, §Scenario 2]
- [x] CHK018 Do requirements state the same-era upstream condition and exactly-one forced-isolated owner outcome without treating command similarity, CWD, environment, or prior legacy ownership as reuse authorization? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §Compatibility matrix; Daemon Control §Identity and owner election requirements]
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements complete for a modern upstream JSON-RPC request, including containment and the prohibited legacy callback, last-active, and broadcast paths? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §FR-010; Lifecycle Quarantine §Boundary error behavior]
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements clear that standard modern logging is optional request-scoped behavior, reaches the sole recipient at most once, and is neither synthesized nor a required readback field? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §FR-011; Owner Status §Required R1 facts; Research §R-07]
- [x] CHK021 Are `input_required`, `inputRequests`, `inputResponses`, and opaque `requestState` requirements clear that host retries are fresh ordinary requests with no mux-authored retry lineage? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §Modern native path, isolated logging, and directionality; Data Model §Native MRTR and subscriptions]
- [x] CHK022 Do requirements define post-loss subscription behavior, including a host-issued fresh `subscriptions/listen`, acknowledgement-before-notification expectation, and the prohibition on automatic re-listen or old-route delivery? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §Modern native path, isolated logging, and directionality; Quickstart §Scenario 5]

## Lifecycle Quarantine and Process Authority

- [x] CHK023 Does the lifecycle contract cover snapshot export and restore, staged restore, and live handoff with an explicit allowed disposition and an explicit prohibition on legacy hydration or attachment? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012; Lifecycle Quarantine §Quarantine matrix]
- [x] CHK024 Are reaper, zero-session cleanup, retry rehydration, and owner-local respawn requirements complete about exact-era continuation versus drain, cold start, or fail-closed disposition? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013; Lifecycle Quarantine §Quarantine matrix]
- [x] CHK025 Are daemon loss, upstream loss, and downstream reconnect requirements complete about terminal work, one-time ephemeral-state clearing, stale-event handling, and no replay of requests, MRTR, progress, or subscriptions? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, FR-014; Lifecycle Quarantine §Universal modern invariants]
- [x] CHK026 Do lifecycle requirements preserve the authority of existing process-generation, inflight, bounded retry, reaper/zero-session, and `RetirementProven` finalization gates rather than introducing a parallel lifecycle controller? [Consistency, Lifecycle Quarantine §Purpose; Data Model §ProcessGeneration and ExistingEphemeralRouteState]
- [x] CHK027 Is the finalization-blocked case specified to retain exact owner authority until proof or explicit failure, avoiding deletion or competing legacy replacement? [Edge Case, Lifecycle Quarantine §Quarantine matrix, §Boundary error behavior]
- [x] CHK028 Are safe cold start, drain/removal, exact-era in-memory continuation, and explicit refusal defined as the only R1 lifecycle outcomes, with no transition to `LegacyReady`? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities; Lifecycle Quarantine §Transition model]

## Minimal Readback and Redaction

- [x] CHK029 Are the required four R1 policy facts specified consistently for every existing `OwnerInfo`-carrying direct owner status, daemon status/list, CLI status, and `mux_list` projection? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015; Owner Status §Required R1 facts]
- [x] CHK030 Is the control echo explicitly distinguished from operator readback so that admission proof and ongoing rollback truth have separate, non-substitutable requirements? [Clarity, Owner Status §Control echo]
- [x] CHK031 Are readiness requirements limited to retaining the meaning of existing fields, while explicitly excluding a new logging field, registry descriptor, topology, lifecycle-state taxonomy, and safe-counter contract? [Scope Consistency, Spec §FR-015; Owner Status §Scope]
- [x] CHK032 Does the redaction requirement enumerate payloads, opaque MRTR state, credentials/tokens/environment values, identities, authorization/tenant material, cache data, and route/request/progress/subscription identifiers across output, errors, logs, and derived forms? [Completeness, Owner Status §Redaction contract]

## Release Evidence, Dependencies, and Exclusions

- [x] CHK033 Are measurable acceptance criteria defined for all seven stated outcomes, including 100%/zero conditions, byte parity, and the distinction between modern proof and legacy parity proof? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK034 Are customer-built-deliverable evidence requirements explicit about exact binary/source identity, operating system, policy spelling, fixture revision, opening bytes, control echo, status snapshots, scenario results, and independent checker identity? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017; Quickstart §Release evidence record]
- [x] CHK035 Is rollback specified as stopping new modern admissions plus draining/removing modern owners, with no live-work conversion to legacy or replay, and are the evidence conditions for rollback completion clear? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §Consumer migration, release, and rollback; Quickstart §Scenario 8]
- [x] CHK036 Are the known-modern-host, same-era-upstream, newline-delimited-frame, released-legacy-baseline, and safe-cold-start assumptions explicitly documented and bounded? [Dependencies & Assumptions, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK037 Do exclusions clearly reserve modern sharing/correlation, cache design, semantic translation, automatic same-shim fallback, subscription continuity, persisted lifecycle transfer, and R3 observability for later work? [Scope Boundary, Spec §Out of scope; Research §Decision Closure]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
